web.how: every route already has its own address; with hosts listed, the web build writes /.well-known/apple-app-site-association when TAC_APPLE_TEAM_ID is set and /.well-known/assetlinks.json when tac.origin and TAC_ANDROID_CERT_SHA256 are set, and /.well-known/windows-app-web-link when TAC_WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PUBLISHER is set, and prints a note for each one it cannot write

macos.note: tac.application.links: the macOS app claims the listed schemes in Info.plist and opens their links at their route, or at start_url when the route is unknown. A signed --release build whose TAC_MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE has the Associated Domains capability embeds the profile and claims the listed hosts with applinks: entries, and the app opens their universal links at their route; other builds leave links to the hosts in the browser. No signed build has opened a link from a hosted domain yet.

windows.note: tac.application.links: the Windows app registers the listed schemes for the current user when it starts (a --release MSIX package declares them as windows.protocol extensions instead), and opens their links at their route, or at start_url when the route is unknown. A link that arrives while the app runs goes to the open window. A --release MSIX package also declares the listed hosts as app URI handlers, and the web build writes /.well-known/windows-app-web-link when TAC_WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PUBLISHER is set; Windows then opens links to the hosts that the shell launches in the app, while links clicked in Edge or another browser stay in it. The unpackaged app leaves links to the hosts in the browser. No package has opened a link from a hosted domain yet.

linux.note: tac.application.links: the Linux .desktop file claims the listed schemes once it is installed, as the release .deb and AppImage do, and the app opens their links at their route, or at start_url when the route is unknown. A link that arrives while the app runs goes to the open window. Linux has no verified web links, so links to the listed hosts stay in the browser.

ios.note: tac.application.links: the iOS app claims the listed schemes in Info.plist and opens their links at their route, or at start_url when the route is unknown. Universal links to the listed hosts need TAC_APPLE_TEAM_ID and a --device or --release build, whose profile has the Associated Domains capability; no signed build has opened one on a device yet. A simulator build opens only the custom schemes.

android.note: tac.application.links: the Android app claims the listed schemes, and https links to the listed hosts with autoVerify, and opens them at their route, or at start_url when the route is unknown. Android verifies the hosts only when each one serves /.well-known/assetlinks.json with the app's signing certificate (TAC_ANDROID_CERT_SHA256); until then it asks which app opens their links.

macos.note: The macOS app's pages load from tachyon-app://bundle, so same-origin requests reach no Yon. Pages and linked Swift HTTP clients reach the Yon at tac.yon.origin, run on macOS by scripts/native/yon-reach-test.mjs (NET1). A linked Rust service's HTTPClient, and any other async linked Rust member, answers HTTP_MISSING there, because the macOS host does not run Rust tasks yet (LR1). The page holds a linked Swift service's stream and socket clients and delivers their messages to it (LS1); a macOS run of that is still owed (yon-reach-test.mjs with a linked Swift stream and socket).

windows.how: the app's pages load from https://tachyon.local, so Yon calls go to tac.yon.origin across origins, from the page and from linked Rust and C# services, and the page holds a linked C# or Rust service's stream and socket clients (NET3, LS1); other absolute URLs go only to the hosts in tac.outgoing.hosts

HTTP calls, streams, sockets and topics from pages and linked Rust services reach the Yon at tac.yon.origin, which lists tachyon://app in server.origins, run under Xvfb and on WSL by scripts/linux/yon-origin-native-test.mjs (NET4, RL1).

ios.note: The iOS app's pages load from tachyon-app://bundle, so same-origin requests reach no Yon. Pages and linked Swift HTTP clients reach the Yon at tac.yon.origin, run on the iOS simulator by scripts/native/yon-reach-test.mjs (NET1). A linked Rust service's HTTPClient, and any other async linked Rust member, answers HTTP_MISSING there, because the iOS host does not run Rust tasks yet (LR1). The page holds a linked Swift service's stream and socket clients and delivers their messages to it (LS1); an iOS simulator run of that is still owed (yon-reach-test.mjs with a linked Swift stream and socket).

android.note: The Android app's pages load from https://appassets.tachyon.local, so same-origin requests reach no Yon. HTTP calls, streams, sockets and topics from pages, and linked Kotlin and Rust HTTP clients, reach the Yon at tac.yon.origin, run on the Android 15 emulator by scripts/android/yon-origin-test.mjs and rust-services-test.mjs (NET2, MR2). The page also holds a linked Kotlin service's stream and socket clients and delivers their messages to it (LS1); an emulator run of that is still owed.
